content:
Apple has recently raised prices on most of its products, but more price hikes are expected next month, covering iPhones and other products.

With the launch of the iPhone 18 series, iPhone prices are expected to rise, and Apple Watch and AirPods may also be affected.

Earlier this summer, Apple had already raised prices on many of its products.

Mac, iPad, Apple TV, HomePod and Vision Pro all saw price increases at the same time.

CEO Tim Cook had previously hinted that price hikes were coming, but the scope of the increases across so many products is still shocking.

Among the first round of price hikes, the only flagship products that were unaffected included:

  • iPhone
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods

At the time, Apple hinted that more price hikes would come in the future, and analysts believe the few products that initially escaped the increases will soon face the same fate.

There is now widespread expectation that Apple will raise iPhone prices at its September iPhone 18 launch event.

According to rumours, the iPhone 18 Pro will have a starting price between US$1,299 and US$1,399, higher than the iPhone 17 Pro's US$1,099.

Apple usually lowers prices on older iPhone models when new phones are launched, but this year the older models are expected to maintain current prices or see only slight increases.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are also likely candidates for price hikes, as the current AI-driven memory crisis will affect watch components.

Finally, AirPods may also see price increases. Although AirPods should be less affected by rising memory and storage chip costs, the chance of a price hike is still lower than for iPhone and Apple Watch.

However, if Apple plans to raise prices across its entire product line, including AirPods, we will have to wait until the September launch event to find out.

What price adjustments do you expect from Apple? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
